metadata.name: touch
metadata.displayName: touch - Create files or update timestamps
metadata.description: Create empty files or update file timestamps

installation.note: touch is a built-in command available on all Linux systems by default

overview.summary: touch creates empty files or updates the access and modification timestamps of existing files. It's commonly used to create placeholder files, update file timestamps for build systems, or create multiple files at once.

syntax.description: Create FILE(s) if they don't exist, or update their timestamps if they do. Multiple files can be created at once.

options.use_case: Update only access time, not modification time
Update only modification time, not access time
Set file timestamp to specific date/time
Copy timestamp from one file to another

output_explanation.format: No output means file was created successfully

elements.meaning: File created (or timestamp updated if exists)

breakdown.behavior: Creates file if it doesn't exist, updates timestamp if it does
breakdown.useful: Common for creating placeholder files, lock files, etc.

output_explanation.notes: Creates empty file. If file already exists, updates its timestamp instead. Use ls -l to verify.

output_explanation.format: No output means all files were created successfully

breakdown.efficient: Creates all files in one command
breakdown.useful: Common for setting up project structure

output_explanation.notes: Creates all specified files. Useful for creating multiple files at once. Can use brace expansion: touch file{1..5}.txt

examples.title: Update file timestamp

output_explanation.format: No output means timestamp was updated

elements.meaning: File's access and modification times updated to current time

breakdown.behavior: If file exists, touch updates its timestamps
breakdown.useful: Trigger build systems, update file metadata
breakdown.verify: Use ls -l to see updated timestamp

output_explanation.notes: Updates file timestamps to current time. Useful for triggering build systems that check file modification times.

examples.use_case: Update file timestamps (trigger builds, update metadata)

examples.title: Set specific timestamp
examples.description: Set file timestamp to specific date/time

output_explanation.format: No output means timestamp was set successfully

breakdown.format: [[CC]YY]MMDDhhmm[.ss] - year, month, day, hour, minute, optional seconds
breakdown.useful: Set specific timestamps for testing, archiving

output_explanation.notes: Sets file timestamp to specific date/time. Format: YYYYMMDDhhmm (year, month, day, hour, minute).

examples.title: Copy timestamp from another file
examples.description: Copy timestamp from source file to target file

output_explanation.format: No output means timestamp was copied successfully

elements.meaning: Use timestamp from source.txt as reference

breakdown.behavior: Copies access and modification times from source to target

output_explanation.notes: Copies timestamp from source file to target file. Useful for maintaining file relationships or synchronizing timestamps.

misconceptions.title: touch only creates files
misconceptions.reality: touch creates files if they don't exist, but also updates timestamps if files already exist. This dual behavior is useful for both creating files and updating metadata.
misconceptions.tip: touch creates files OR updates timestamps. If file exists, it updates the timestamp instead of creating a new file.

common_pitfalls.description: Accidentally creating files in current directory instead of intended location
common_pitfalls.solution: Always specify full path or verify current directory with pwd before using touch.

common_pitfalls.description: Worrying that touch will overwrite file contents
common_pitfalls.solution: touch never overwrites file contents - it only creates empty files or updates timestamps. Your data is safe.

related_commands.relationship: Create directories; touch creates files, mkdir creates directories
related_commands.description: Create directories (complement to touch for files)

related_commands.relationship: View files; touch creates, ls shows files with timestamps
related_commands.description: List files with timestamps (ls -l shows touch-created files)

best_practices: Use touch to create empty placeholder files
Use touch to update file timestamps for build systems
Use touch with brace expansion: touch file{1..10}.txt
Use -r to copy timestamps between files
Use -t to set specific timestamps when needed
performance_tips: Creating multiple files at once is efficient
No performance impact - just file system metadata operations

additional_notes.dual_behavior: touch creates files if they don't exist, or updates timestamps if they do
additional_notes.empty_files: touch creates empty files (0 bytes) - use editors to add content
additional_notes.timestamp_format: Use -t with format: [[CC]YY]MMDDhhmm[.ss] for specific timestamps
additional_notes.common_use: Common patterns: touch file.txt (create), touch -r source.txt target.txt (copy timestamp), touch file{1..5}.txt (multiple files)
